name: Belovode copper smelting
summary: Slag and slag-coated pottery at the Vinča settlement of Belovode show people extracting copper from ore around 5000 BCE, among Europe's early evidence of smelting.
description: Copper-bearing slag and slagged ceramic sherds document local extraction of copper from ore at Belovode. A separately excavated cluster in Trench 18 supports the use of manganese-rich copper ores and suggests a pit with ceramic lining.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: One settlement's slag showing metal newly won from ore, within a Vinča copper-smelting practice that continued; scores imply tier 2, below the reviewed tier 1.

date.label: by c. 4650 BCE
date.basis: The Trench 3 D/Gradac occupation is approximately 5000–4650 BCE; slag and sherds support an inferred local smelting context, not a hard earliest operation date. The horizon and end are approximate.

events.statement: Copper-bearing slag and slagged ceramics in the dated Belovode occupation imply local extractive smelting by the end of the cited horizon.
events.caveats: Small samples and contextual dating constrain a horizon; no specific first use, furnace form, economic exchange or global priority is established.

evidence.locator: pp. 13–14, Trench No. 3; context and smelting debris
evidence.supports: The physical debris comes from a dated settlement sequence and is interpreted as ore smelting.

date.label: c. 5000–4650 BCE
date.basis: Trench 3, occupation horizon D / Gradac phase; archaeological phase range reported by excavators.

events.statement: Copper-bearing slag and slagged ceramic sherds document extraction of copper from ore at a Vinča settlement.
events.caveats: Small debris survives; convincing smelting installations were not identified. This node makes no sole-origin or universal-earliest claim.

evidence.locator: pp. 13–14; Trench No. 3; cached text lines 408–424 and 474–504

date.label: 4724–4555 cal BCE, associated Feature 6 sample
date.basis: Published 2σ radiocarbon range for the animal-bone sample MAMS23380 associated with Feature 6 in Trench 18.

events.statement: Slag and a slagged sherd were excavated around Feature 6 at Belovode. The analyses support the use of manganese-rich copper ore. The cluster of debris and a burnt, bowl-shaped feature suggest a pottery-lined smelting pit.
events.caveats: The sample dates the associated feature. The lining and precise use of Feature 6 remain archaeological inferences.

evidence.supports: Distinct debris and an associated radiocarbon date in the 2012–2013 excavation.

evidence.locator: pp. 133–138 and 149–151, sherd analysis and conclusion
evidence.supports: Nearby slagged ceramics support the pit-lining interpretation and analyses corroborate the ore characteristics.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. Trench 3, occupation horizon D / Gradac phase; archaeological phase range reported by excavators. Small debris survives; convincing smelting installations were not identified. This node makes no sole-origin or universal-earliest claim. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.rationale: The archaeometallurgical debris indicates productive local operation rather than the much later date of excavation.
community_entry.proxy_reason: The inference is from historical production residue to local metallurgical activity; the first act and community size are not directly observed.
community_entry.caveats: Small samples and contextual dating constrain a horizon; no specific first use, furnace form, economic exchange or global priority is established.

caveats: Trench 3 yielded small debris and no confirmed smelting installation. A later excavation at Trench 18 identified a possible pottery-lined pit. The geological source of the ore and the transmission of the technique remain unresolved.

unresolved.note: Seek a geologically matched, dated extraction context and in situ ceramic lining with diagnostic smelting residues before assigning a specific source or installation.

evidence.supports: Field contexts and distinct metallurgy samples support local smelting and narrow questions about the installation and ore.
